message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|-----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Atomic Number | 1 |
| | Symbol | H |
| | Molar Mass | ≈ 1.008 g·mol⁻¹ (protium) |
| | Electron Configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopic Forms | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H/D), Tritium (^3H/T) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionisation Energy | 13.598 eV (first IE) |
| | Electron Affinity | 0.7547 eV |
| **Physical State (STP)** | Phase | Di‑molecular gas (H₂) |
| | Boiling Point | –252.87 °C (21 K) |
| | Melting Point | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| | Density | 0.08988 kg/m³ (at 25 °C, 101.325 kPa) |
| | Specific Heat Capacity (gas) | 28.836 J/(kg·K) |
| | Speed of Sound | ~1275 m/s (in pure H₂) |
| | Spectral Lines | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible) |
| **Chemical Behavior** | Bond Type | Covalent (diatomic H₂) |
| | Oxidation States | +1 (most stable), -1 (hydride ions) |
| | Common Compounds | Water (H₂O), Hydrochloric acid (HCl), Ammonia (NH₃), Methane (CH₄), Hydrides (LiH, NaH…) |
| | Flammability | Extremely high; explosive limits ~4%–75% in air |
| | Standard Enthalpy of Formation | ΔfH°(H₂(g)) = 0 kcal/mol (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs Free Energy of Formation | ΔfG°(H₂(g)) = 0 kcal/mol |
| | Solubility in water | Low (~9 mg/L at 25 °C) |
| **Nuclear & Quantum Features** | Nuclear Spin | Protium I=½, Deuterium I=1, Tritium I=½ |
| | Hyperfine Splitting | 1420 MHz line (21 cm radio astronomy) |
| | Magnetic Moment | Proton magnetic moment ≈ 2.7928 μ_N |

---

### Quick Takeaways

* **Lightest Element:** Only one proton and usually one electron → very small size and low mass.
* **Highly Reactive Gas:** Easily forms covalent bonds; reacts vigorously with oxygen, halogens, metals, and many organic molecules.
* **Isotope Diversity:** Deuterium used in heavy-water reactors; tritium appears naturally in cosmic rays and is produced in fusion research.
* **Spectroscopic Importance:** Its simple electronic transitions make it ideal for studying quantum mechanics and astrophysical plasmas.
* **Industrial Role:** Primary feedstock for ammonia synthesis (via Haber process); key component in fuel cells when paired with oxygen to generate electricity and water.

Feel free to ask more specific questions—whether you’re curious about hydrogen’s role in stellar nucleosynthesis, its use in clean-energy technologies, or detailed spectroscopic data!
